## This game

A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.

I’ll read the last two reviews, keep the opponent at 20k, and play White through to completion. I’ll focus on developing enough territory early and checking actual eye space, then save the game and lessons for the next session.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.

const review=`# Game 172: White vs 20k — B+16

Played 2026-10-07. Chinese area scoring, komi7, simple ko.
White68/Black69 passes ended the game; closing board confirms B+16, next70.
Area Black52/White29, neutral0; all final stones retained reproduces52-29-7=16.
No scoring dead removal needed. Physical captures Black16/White0.
Simple ko at J2 after Black49 J1, resolved by Black51 J2. No invalid move or resignation.
Completed20k:28 wins/133 losses/6 draws; game87 unfinished/excluded. Retain20k.

## Evidence

Read171/170 and consulted169 before selecting20k, returning Black1 E5.
All69 actual moves replay legally and match all36 raw boards, captures, next numbers and ko markers.
Selection,34 play responses and closing confirmation saved individually before the next dependent Go action.
Aggregate log, SGF, recorder, inspector, final inspection, verifier, verification, review and focus saved.
Manual move choices and unplayed reading only; code inspected current boards and replayed actual history.
No engine, Monte Carlo, future-sequence search, move-selecting/ranking/recommending program or delegation.
Game52 scoring discrepancy and99/106 raw-evidence limits remain separate.

The contemporary G9 note is wrong as a decision: it checked the opposing H9 atari but omitted White's resulting sole E9.
The next recorded note acknowledges the resulting capture. No subsequent successful defense is claimed.

## Exact moves

${load("log").moves.map(m=>m.n+" "+m.color+" "+m.move).join(", ")}.

## Three early bases did not preserve three viable rooms

C3 and C6 began separate left footholds; G3 supplied a separate lower-right base at6.
F3 actually joined G3. C4 joined C3; C5 actually joined C4/C6.
D6 joined C6, but E6 capped it; D7/C7 capped above.

Before10, exact disjoint OPEN43 reference:
ABC allrows27 + D/E/F/G/H/J rows1-2 twelve + F/G/H/J row3 four.
Entirely unsecured, no completed life, upper-left nine without a White boundary.
C7 cap prompted a realistic34 reference after subtracting upperABC7-9nine.
This was already below White38 with all81 assigned, and H3 contested the right endpoint.
The later connected left expansion recovered seven of those upper-left nine; do not subtract all nine from the final ledger.

G7 at16 began upper-right development earlier than game170's G7 at30.
F7/F8/F9 actually joined and retained the top endpoint against E7/E8.
H8 at24 was SEPARATE, diagonal to G7. G8 at26 actually joined it to F8/G7.
Black H7/H6 capped rightward, and J8 was initially isolated.
One connected upper room was still not two eyes.
F6 at28 joined F7, seeking a route down F5/F4 to F3.
Black F5 at29 joined E5/G5 and closed that route.
Earlier development alone did not create life; the opposing caps still removed width.

## J9 self-atari, then G9 self-atari: inspect the moving chain first

After29, upper WHITE SEVEN F6/F7/F8/F9/G7/G8/H8 had exactly E9/G9/H9 liberties.
J8 Black had H8(White), J7 and J9 liberties, hence J7/J9.
White30 J9 was SEPARATE, with soleH9. It ataried J8 to J7 but also self-ataried its own isolated stone.
Black31 H9 captured J9, reopened J9 for both H9 and J8, and occupied an upper White liberty.
Upper seven now had exactly E9/G9; Black H9 had G9/J9.

White32 G9 actually joined the upper main and ataried H9 to J9.
But it also left White EIGHT with soleE9.
Black33 E9 joined E8 and captured all eight.
The manually imagined H9/J9/J8 capture depended on Black saving H9 instead of taking the much larger White group.
This was a concrete own-chain liberty omission, not an unavoidable trade or an established best move.
Even an opponent atari does not force a reply when the attacker can be captured first.

Rebuild after every capture: H9's capture reopened J9 and removed H9 from White's available liberties.
Counting only the threatened enemy chain missed the decisive change.
Before any atari, identify every friendly chain the move joins, the resulting full liberty set,
and whether the opponent can capture that chain immediately.

## Lower-right caps and timely abandonment

D3 joined C3; Black D2 invaded underneath.
C2 joined C3 before E2 joined the Black main.
F2 joined F3; G4 capped above. G2 joined F2/G3; H2 joined H3 and capped rightward.
H1 at42 was SEPARATE with G1/J1; G1 at44 actually joined it to G2/main.
The lower six F2/F3/G1/G2/G3/H1 had only F1/F4/J1, no empty eye region.
D1 joined D2 and blocked the bottom route toward the left group.

J2 at46 was SEPARATE, diagonal to H1. J3 capped it, leaving soleJ1.
Manual audit: J1 would join J2/H1 but leave the main only F1/F4.
F1 would lead only to E1, which borders Black D1/E2; F4 borders Black E4/F5/G4.
No independent room or viable continuation was identified.
Stopped extending and played C1 to preserve the left endpoint instead.
This is a local audit, not an exhaustive whole-board proof.

Black49 J1 captured J2, creating simple ko at J2.
White50 B6 was played elsewhere; Black51 J2 joined J1/J3/H2 and resolved ko.
Black53 F1 closed another liberty of the lower six, leaving soleF4.
White F4 would have no liberty and capture no adjacent Black chain: suicide; it was not submitted.
Black55 F4 captured all six and reopened their six points.
The physical captures are separate from scoring removal; no dead stones remain displayed.

## Connected left expansion and real independent rooms

C1 actually joined C2 and retained the first-line endpoint against D1.
B6 joined C6. B7/B8 actually extended that same chain past C7.
These were connected moves, not separate diagonal hanes.
C8 joined B8 and expanded above C7.
Black C9 capped above; B9 joined B8 and retained the top endpoint.
Black D9 joined C9/E9.
D8 joined C8 and gained one mixed boundary point; it was not an eye because D7/D9/E8 are Black.
Black D5 occupied one central point; D4 joined C4/D3 and gained the other mixed point.

At63 the left main15 stones had one14-point room A1-A9/B1-B5:29 area.
B5 joined C5 and began a horizontal divider.
A5 joined B5 and completed it, separating:
upper A6/A7/A8/A9 four-point room;
lower A1/A2/A3/A4/B1/B2/B3/B4 eight-point room.
Both have only the SAME White physical chain as boundary.
White17 stones+12 empties=29; the divider preserved Chinese area and proved unconditional life.
No viable outside gain was identified. White68/Black69 passed.

## Final inventory and exact score

White17, ONE chain:
A5/B5/B6/B7/B8/B9/C1/C2/C3/C4/C5/C6/C8/D3/D4/D6/D8.
Upper4/lower8 empty rooms as above:29.

Black34 in FOUR physical chains:
main31 C7/C9/D1/D2/D5/D7/D9/E2/E3/E4/E5/E6/E7/E8/E9/F4/F5/F8/G4/G5/G6/H2/H3/H4/H6/H7/J1/J2/J3/J7/J8;
isolated H9, J5, F1.
Black18 empty points:
F6/F7/F9/G7/G8/G9/H8 seven; J9/J6/H5/J4 four;
F2/F3/G1/G2/G3/H1 six; E1 one.
Some rooms border several Black chains; do not invent individual two-eye proofs for every isolate.
All stones retained matches official B+16; neutral0.

Exact initial43 ledger:
lose C7/C9 two;
lose all sixteen initially referenced points outside ABC (D/E/F/G/H/J rows1-2 and F/G/H/J row3);
gain D3/D4/D6/D8 four outside that reference.
43-18+4=29.
The failed upper group and J9 are outside the original43, so their captures are not extra subtractions from it.
No Chinese-area capture bonus.

Capture events:
Black31 H9 took J9 one;33 E9 upper eight;
49 J1 took J2 one;55 F4 lower six. Total16/0.

## Carry forward

Retain20k:28 wins/133 losses/6 draws;87 unfinished/excluded.
Read172/171; consult170 for similar failed upper room and169/165/154 for actual joins and broad rooms.
Make the own-chain liberty check BEFORE enemy-atari reading.
J9 soleH9 and G9 soleE9 are immediate current-position checks that need no engine or sequence search.
An earlier separate base still requires real eye room after the first opposing cap.
Preserve the useful connected B6-B9/C8/D8 expansion and B5/A5 divider.
Winning width remains unresolved: successful left29 alone cannot replace two failed bases.
No move or alternative opening is established optimal.
`;
store("review",review);text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: game-172.md\n+"+review.trimEnd().replace(/\n/g,"\n+")+"\n*** End Patch"));

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.
